title: What every part of The Great String War carries

entities.title: Say what is memory and what is not
entities.summary: Every part carries the date line and opens with a short note saying what in it is memory and what is not.
entities.statement: Each part has, under its title and italic subtitle, the date line "Built at OZ, 1998–2002 · Written November 2026" and a rule, then a quoted note "Part N of 11 in *The Great String War*" saying which of its contents are memory and which are general knowledge, checked in 2026. The README says the notes should stay when the parts are published.
entities.rationale: The story is told from memory a quarter of a century later, beside general knowledge checked in 2026; the reader is told which is which.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the eleven working copies has the date line and the rule under its subtitle.
Each opens with the quoted note naming its part number of 11 and what is memory.

relationships.description: The site's copies dropped the notes.

entities.title: Refer to other parts by title
entities.summary: Parts refer to each other by title, in italics, so that the references read the same here and on the site.
entities.statement: A reference from one part to another is the other part's title in italics, such as *Tricks of the string trade*, not a file name or a part number.
acceptanceCriteria: No working copy links to another part's file; each names it by its title in italics.
